verdict: LEARNED PERTURBATION SIMILARITY from gene features (no peeking at the held-out KO), K562, 126 held-out knockouts, specific-mover recall@50: TIDE null 0.241 -> fixed PHYS graph 0.373 -> LEARNED 0.398 -> ORACLE* ceiling 0.616. HONEST READ: the learned annotation-similarity BARELY beats the fixed physical graph (0.398 vs 0.373, only +0.025, closing just 10% of the graph->oracle head-room). This is a NEGATIVE-ish result and I am reporting it as one: hand-crafted STATIC ANNOTATION features (complex + GO-BP/CC/MF + pathway + PPI-neighbourhood + dependency + degree + compartment) add almost nothing over the raw physical graph for predicting which knockouts behave alike. The large oracle head-room (behavioural similarity IS there and IS shared) is NOT reachable from these annotations. WHAT THIS RULES IN/OUT: it rules OUT 'just engineer more annotation features' as the path to the oracle, and points to a richer REPRESENTATION -- learned gene embeddings, sequence/structure (ESM), or ultimately co-perturbation profiles (which is the oracle, i.e. you need measured neighbours). NEXUS/structural interaction magnitude can still enter as a feature here, but the bar is now explicit and high: it must beat 0.398, and annotation features already saturate near the graph, so it would have to add genuinely ORTHOGONAL behavioural signal. CAVEATS: modest test set (126 KOs); single-KO, within-one-cell-type, one steady-state-mRNA readout; says nothing about combinations, mutations, drugs, cross-cell-type, or a real cancer genotype.
